text: Renamed the `OrderStatus` enum values to SCREAMING_CASE across 23 files and updated the GraphQL schema to match. Type check and the 312 unit tests pass.

Added structured error logging to the payment webhook: each error now carries the request ID and the Stripe event type, so you can grep for a single delivery. No behaviour change for successful events.

Implemented the role-based permission check for the reports page. Admins and analysts see the export button; viewers get a read-only table. Covered all three roles in `reports.permissions.test.tsx` (9 tests, all green).

Pulled the latest main into your branch. Git flagged a conflict in `src/theme/tokens.ts` because both sides added a color; I kept both entries and sorted them alphabetically. Build and Storybook both compile.
The flaky `upload.spec.ts` test that failed twice yesterday is now deterministic: it was racing the file chooser, and I now await the `filechooser` event before clicking. 25 consecutive runs passed.

Benchmark results after switching the JSON serializer:

| Payload | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 1 KB | 0.42 ms | 0.18 ms |
| 100 KB | 31 ms | 12 ms |
| 1 MB | 340 ms | 118 ms |

Roughly 2.7x faster across the board, with identical output bytes.
Done. The README now documents the `--dry-run` flag.

## Summary
- Moved the cron jobs from `node-cron` to BullMQ repeatable jobs
- Each job now has a dead-letter queue, so failures are retried 3 times before parking
- Added a `/admin/queues` dashboard behind the existing admin guard

Zero failures in a 2-hour soak test with 10k jobs.
No errors, no warnings: `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` is clean after removing the two unused imports in `src/parser/mod.rs`.

Pinned Python to 3.11.9 in `.python-version` and bumped `pydantic` from 1.10.13 to 2.7.1. The v2 migration needed the `Config` classes replaced with `model_config`; the API responses are byte-identical in the snapshot tests.

The reason the modal closed on Safari is that `pointerdown` fires before `focusout` there, so the outside-click handler can't tell the target is inside. I switched the handler to `click`, which fires after focus settles, and the modal stays open in Safari 17.4 and Chrome.

Plan for the search feature:

1. Add a `tsvector` column on `articles` with a GIN index
2. Backfill it in batches of 5,000 rows
3. Expose `GET /search?q=` with ranking by `ts_rank`
4. Add a 250 ms debounce on the client

Starting with the migration now.
Locked down the S3 bucket: public access is now blocked and the CloudFront origin uses OAC, so direct object URLs return Access Denied while the CDN URLs keep working. Verified both with curl.

## What I did

The mobile app crashed on launch for users upgrading from 4.x because the persisted Redux state had an old shape. I added a migration step (version 5) to `redux-persist` that maps `user.prefs` to the new `settings` slice and drops the deprecated `theme` key.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the migration with three real snapshots taken from 4.2, 4.6 and 4.9
- Manually upgraded an emulator from 4.9.3 to the new build: no crash, settings preserved
- Fresh install still works

## Notes

- The migration is idempotent, so users who already hit the crash and reinstalled are unaffected
- I left a TODO to delete the migration after 5.3 ships, i.e. once 4.x drops below 1% of sessions

All 148 tests pass.
Deleted the three unused feature flags (`newCheckout`, `betaSearch`, `darkModeV1`) and their dead branches. Bundle size dropped by 14 KB gzipped.
Updated the Dockerfile to a multi-stage build on `node:20-alpine`. Image size went from 1.1 GB to 182 MB and the container still passes the health check.
Reviewed the PR as requested. It looks solid: the only nit is that `formatCurrency` hard-codes `en-US`, but that matches the rest of the codebase, so I didn't flag it as blocking.
The `orders` table has 40M rows, so adding the column with a default will lock it for several minutes. Should I add it as nullable first and backfill in the background instead?

Before I wire up notifications, which channel should be the default for new users?

- Email only
- Push only
- Both, with a daily digest

Everything else for the settings page is done.

text: I've prepared the release notes for 3.0 in `CHANGELOG.md`. I need you to confirm the breaking-change list before I tag the release.

2. Do you want me to keep the old `amount` field during the transition?

The two caching approaches have different trade-offs, so this one is your call:

| | Redis | In-process LRU |
|---|---|---|
| Shared across pods | yes | no |
| Extra infra | yes | no |
| Latency | ~1 ms | ~0.01 ms |

Want me to push the branch?

## Why was the page slow?

Every row rendered its own `<Tooltip>` with a portal, so 2,000 rows meant 2,000 portals.

## What changed?

One shared tooltip now follows the hovered row. Render time dropped from 1.8 s to 0.2 s, e.g. the 2k-row table now scrolls at 60 fps vs. about 12 fps before.

Fixed the optional-chaining crash:

```js
const city = user?.address?.city ?? 'unknown';
```

The original error was "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')" and it no longer reproduces with the fixture from issue #412.
Node 18.20.4 reaches end-of-life soon, and the Lambda runtime vs. the local `.nvmrc` already differ (20.11.1 vs. 18.20.4). Should I standardise on 20.x everywhere, e.g. in CI, Docker and `.nvmrc`?

Q: Does the importer handle BOM-prefixed CSVs? A: Yes, as of this change it strips the BOM. Q: Does it handle semicolon delimiters? A: Not yet. Do you want semicolon support in this PR, or a separate one?
